accepted.question_text: Give a mathematically rigorous treatment of the axioms of physics, including an axiomatic treatment of probability with limit theorems suitable for the foundations of statistical physics and a rigorous theory of the limiting processes that pass from an atomistic description of matter to the laws of motion for continua.
accepted.context_brief: Hilbert problem 6 and foundations of statistical physics

evidence.quote: Mathematical treatment of the axioms of physics. In particular I the axiomatic treatment of probability with limit theorems for the foundation of statistical physics I the rigorous theory of limiting processes "which lead from the atomistic view to the laws of motion of continua."

accepted.question_text: Determine whether P equals NP, meaning whether every decision problem whose proposed solution can be verified in polynomial time can also itself be solved in polynomial time.

evidence.quote: Does P = NP? I It asks whether every problem whose solution can be quickly verified (technically, verified in polynomial time) can also be solved quickly (again, in polynomial time).

accepted.question_text: Establish the existence of quantum Yang–Mills theory in a mathematically rigorous way and prove that it has a positive mass gap, despite the underlying classical field theory having solutions that propagate at the speed of light and the physical picture involving color confinement of gluons into massive bound states.

evidence.quote: Yang–Mills existence and mass gap. I establish the existence of the quantum Yang–Mills theory and a mass gap rigorously. I As a classical field theory, its solutions propagate at the speed of light and so its quantum version describes massless gluons. I The so-called mass gap is the problem that color confinement only allows bound states of gluons, which form massive particles.

accepted.question_text: For the Newtonian N-body problem with gravitating particles, prove that the set of initial conditions that do not yield global solutions has measure zero, and determine whether noncollisional singularities can occur.

evidence.quote: Existance for Newtonian gravitating particles. I prove that the set of initial conditions which fails to have global solutions is of measure zero. I existence of noncollisional singularities in the Newtonian N-body problem.

accepted.question_text: Develop a comprehensive theory of the long-time behavior of dynamical systems that also explains the onset of turbulence and the regime of fully developed turbulence.

evidence.quote: Develop a comprehensive theory of the long time behavior of dynamical systems including a theory of the onset of, and of fully developed, turbulence.

accepted.question_text: Prove that every Yang–Mills field on the 4-sphere S4 is either self-dual or anti-self-dual.

evidence.quote: Prove that any YM field on S4 is either self-dual or antiself-dual.

accepted.question_text: Prove that, for a fixed Pontryagin number, the moduli space of self-dual Yang–Mills fields on the 4-sphere S4 is connected.

evidence.quote: Prove that the moduli space of the self-dual fields on S4 with a fixed Pontryagin number is connected.

accepted.question_text: Give a mathematically precise formulation of the renormalization group for n-dimensional Ising-type systems and prove universality, in particular that the critical exponents for three-dimensional nearest-neighbor Ising models do not depend on anisotropy in the bond strengths along the three coordinate directions.

evidence.quote: Formulation of the renormalization group and proof of universality. I develop a mathematically precise version of the renormalization transformations for n-dimensional Ising-type systems. I in particular, show that the critical exponents in the three-dimensional Ising models with nearest neighbor coupling but different bond strengths in the three directions are independent of the ratios of these bond strengths.

accepted.question_text: Construct a precise mathematical formulation of quantum chromodynamics and resolve whether nonlinear quantum field theory in three spatial dimensions plus one time dimension can be made into a genuine mathematical theory, including whether there exist nontrivial renormalizable but not super-renormalizable quantum field theories, whether quantum electrodynamics is inconsistent, and whether nontrivial lattice cutoff theories exist.

evidence.quote: Problems in QFT I give a precise mathematical construction of quantum chromodynamics, the model of strong interaction physics. I construct any non-trivial renormalizable but not super-renormalizable quantum field theory. I prove that quantum electrodynamics is not a consistent theory. I prove that a non-trivial lattice cutoff theories theory does not exist.

accepted.question_text: Justify major approximation schemes in general relativity rigorously by proving an approximate-solution theorem for the vacuum Einstein equations in a suitable norm, showing that solutions of the linearized Einstein equations about Minkowski space stay close to nonflat exact solutions, determining the range of validity of post-Newtonian and post-Minkowskian asymptotic expansions, and proving the existence of a limit in which solutions of the Einstein equations reduce to Newtonian spacetimes.

evidence.quote: Validity of approximations in GR I Prove an "approximate solution" result for the (vacuum) Einstein equations in some suitable norm that would provide a good way to evaluate approximate/ asymptotic and numerical solutions. I Show that a solution of the linearized (about Minkowski space) Einstein equations is close to a (nonflat) exact solution. I Determine the range of validity of the post- Newtonian and post-Minkowskian asymptotic expansions. I Prove rigorously the existence of a limit in which solutions of the Einstein equations reduce to Newtonian spacetimes.

accepted.question_text: Resolve several causality and singularity questions in general relativity: whether there exists a timelike geodesically complete inextendible Lorentz manifold satisfying an energy condition and containing a trapped surface in a partial Cauchy surface; whether a weak Cauchy surface in a globally hyperbolic spacetime with suitable energy conditions can contain an inextendible null geodesic; whether a cosmological spacetime satisfying the timelike convergence condition must either be timelike geodesically incomplete or split isometrically as R × M3 and therefore be static; whether a singularity theorem can be proved assuming the dominant energy condition instead of the timelike convergence condition; and what the weakest metric smoothness assumptions are that still give uniqueness in the initial-value problem for maximizing geodesics.
accepted.context_brief: Causality and singularity in general relativity

evidence.quote: Causality and singularity in GR I Is there a timelike geodesically complete inextendible Lorentz manifold satisfying an energy condition and having a partial Cauchy surface which contains a trapped surface? I Show that a weak Cauchy surface in a globally hyperbolic spacetime satisfying suitable energy conditions cannot contain an inextendible null geodesic. I Prove that a ‘cosmological spacetime’ satisfying the timelike convergence condition is either timelike geodesically incomplete or it splits as R × M3 isometrically (and is thus static). I Prove a singularity theorem assuming the dominant energy condition rather than the timelike convergence condition. I Determine the weakest condition on the smoothness of the metric in the initial value problem for maximizing geodesics to have a unique solution.

accepted.question_text: Show that there is no vacuum equilibrium configuration in general relativity containing more than one black hole.

evidence.quote: Show that there is no vacuum equilibrium configuration involving more than one black hole.

accepted.question_text: Find an exact solution of the Einstein equations representing two orbiting bodies, and determine whether the two-body system is unstable in Einstein gravity.

evidence.quote: Find an exact solution of the Einstein equations which represents two orbiting bodies. Is the 2-body system unstable in Einstein gravity?

accepted.question_text: Prove the weak cosmic censorship conjecture, namely that for generic initial data the maximal Cauchy development has a complete future null infinity, so that singularities are never visible from future null infinity and are hidden behind black-hole event horizons.

evidence.quote: Prove the weak cosmic censorship conjecture. I The weak cosmic censorship hypothesis asserts there can be no singularity visible from future null infinity. In other words, singularities need to be hidden from an observer at infinity by the event horizon of a black hole. I Mathematically, the conjecture states that, for generic initial data, the maximal Cauchy development possesses a complete future null infinity.

accepted.question_text: Either prove the Penrose inequality in full generality or produce a counterexample. The inequality bounds the mass of a spacetime in terms of the total area of its black holes, generalizing the positive mass theorem, and its truth or failure is closely tied to weak cosmic censorship.

evidence.quote: Find a proof of the Penrose inequality or present a counterexample in the general case. I This inequality estimates the mass of a spacetime in terms of the total area of its black holes and is a generalization of the positive mass theorem I Violation of this inequality would constitute a counterexample to weak cosmic censorship, while a proof of this inequality would provide evidence in favor of weak cosmic censorship.

accepted.question_text: Prove the stability of the Kerr–Newman black hole.

evidence.quote: Prove the stability of the Kerr-Newman black hole.

accepted.question_text: Determine when a four-dimensional spacetime is explicitly reconstructible from its scalar curvature invariants, and determine a minimal set of such invariants sufficient for that reconstruction.

evidence.quote: Determine when a 4D spacetime can be explicitly constructed from its scalar curvature invariants and determine the minimal set of such invariants.

accepted.question_text: Give a rigorous proof of the geodesic hypothesis in general relativity by showing that test particles of negligible mass move along spacetime geodesics, and make mathematically precise the limiting process in which the particle mass becomes negligible.

evidence.quote: Prove that test particles move on spacetime geodesics. I Geodesic hypothesis: One of the postulates of GR is that point particles with negligible mass will travel along geodesics of the spacetime. I The main problem is how to make the process of "taking the negligible mass limit" rigorous.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether black holes are unique in higher-dimensional general relativity.

evidence.quote: Determine the uniqueness of black holes in higher dimensions.

accepted.question_text: Determine the stability properties of higher-dimensional black holes.

evidence.quote: Determine the stability of higher dimensional black holes.

accepted.question_text: Prove a cosmic no-hair theorem for generic inhomogeneous spacetimes.

evidence.quote: Prove a cosmic no-hair theorem in generic inhomogeneous space￾times.

accepted.question_text: Provide a rigorous mathematical definition of averaging in general relativity, where the large-scale gravitational field equations are obtained by averaging or coarse-graining the Einstein field equations, and resolve the associated averaging and fitting problems that are crucial for the interpretation of cosmological data.

evidence.quote: Provide a rigorous mathematical definition for averaging in GR. I The gravitational field equations on large scales are obtained by averaging or coarse graining the Einstein field equations of GR. I The averaging problem in cosmology is crucial for the correct interpretation of cosmological data. I The so-called fitting problem is perhaps the most important unsolved problem in mathematical cosmology.

evidence.quote: Resolve the black hole information paradox.

needs_review.question_text_raw: The cosmological constant problem and dark energy.

evidence.quote: The cosmological constant problem and dark energy.

needs_review.question_text_raw: Formulate a fully consistent theory of QG.

evidence.quote: Formulate a fully consistent theory of QG.
